source_claim_verbatim: 随机游走向布朗运动的强逼近
canonical_statement: Leading candidate: for centered variance-one i.i.d. real increments satisfying a suitable exponential-moment condition, there is a coupling of copies of the increments with a standard Brownian motion for which the maximum discrepancy between partial sums and Brownian motion at integer times admits the KMT logarithmic strong-approximation bound; the exact quantitative primary-source variant is not yet frozen.
statement_blocker: The repository wording does not fix the original paper/theorem, moment hypothesis, coupling convention, quantitative constants and tail inequality, or whether only the almost-sure O(log n) consequence is intended.
domain_and_universes: Candidate domain: real-valued random variables on probability spaces and a real standard Brownian motion; exact source and target probability spaces, sigma-algebras, and Lean universes are unfrozen.
quantifiers: law of a centered variance-one real increment satisfying the source-prescribed exponential-moment hypothesis
existence of a coupling probability space
coupled increment sequence and standard Brownian motion
integer horizon n and, for a quantitative form, deviation parameter x
constants depending only on the increment law or its moment data
hypotheses: mean zero and variance one normalization
the coupled increments have the required marginal law
the coupled continuous process is standard Brownian motion
conclusion: A source-exact logarithmic uniform coupling error bound, potentially as an exponential tail inequality implying an almost-sure O(log n) discrepancy.
candidate_scope_families: scalar partial-sum coupling with an exponential deviation bound
the almost-sure O(log n) strong-invariance-principle consequence
extensions to independent non-identically distributed or multidimensional variables
empirical-distribution/empirical-process approximation treated in the original paper series
excluded_claims: Weak convergence in Donsker's invariance principle does not discharge a pathwise logarithmic coupling bound
A Skorokhod embedding without the KMT error estimate does not discharge the root
No multidimensional or empirical-process theorem is silently substituted for the repository's random-walk wording
A structure taking the desired coupling estimate as an assumption is not a proof of the theorem
excluded_degenerate_cases: Zero variance, missing centering, horizons below the source range, distributions without the selected moment condition, and continuous-time interpolation are open boundary decisions, not silently accepted cases.
foundation_profile: Classical measure-theoretic probability and choice may be required for coupling constructions; the rev-5.6 accepted principle set is open.
tcb_profile: Lean 4 kernel plus a pinned mathlib dependency closure; exact versions and transitive dependencies are open.
computation_profile: No simulation, numerical experiment, oracle, or external computation is credited at intake.
source_revisions: Primary bibliographic candidates and unresolved mappings are recorded in source_statement_crosswalk.md; immutable source files, exact theorem/page anchors, and errata status remain open.
freshness_and_revocation_policy: Invalidate on changes to the selected source theorem, canonical claim, Lean target, imports/toolchain, foundation/TCB policy, or rev-5.6 standard.
status_boundary: This intake identifies and bounds the KMT theorem family. It does not freeze an exact quantitative statement, establish a Lean anchor, accept a human-source proof crosswalk, or prove the theorem.
